title: ARC live-path per-game lookup enumeration (adapter-free proxy fidelity audit)
inference_substrate_note: Static import-closure analysis (ast) over the two canonical live entrypoints, plus a CPU-only construction-time delivery probe that instruments the CALLEES and reads the caller off the stack. No LLM was loaded, no GPU was touched, no game was played, no scored/online run occurred. GGUF strings elsewhere in the repo are not a live-inference claim here.
solve_provenance_note: This is a code-audit of a live mechanism plus a construction-only differential probe. No hidden game was played and no level was solved, so this is neither live_agent_self_discovery nor a solve claim of any kind.

preconditions_checked.note: deliberately not used; GPU 1 is owned by a concurrent workflow and was not touched

method.closure: ast walk of absolute, relative and function-level imports from each canonical live entrypoint, mirroring scripts/arc_orphan_solver_lint.py's closure rule
entrypoints: scripts/arc_loop_solve.py (OfflineSolver + GameAdapter; the offline DEV TWIN)
method.delivery_probe: each candidate lookup CALLEE was monkeypatched; E3AgentPolicy was then constructed for a PUBLIC id (sb26) and a synthetic HIDDEN id (zz99hiddengame); the caller was read off the stack. Availability is not delivery -- only sites that fired are reported as delivered.
method.probe_n_note: n=2 game ids is a DELIVERY witness, not a statistical sample. No p-value is claimed anywhere in this artifact because no comparative outcome measurement was run -- this phase is enumeration only, per the task's 'do NOT change behaviour in this phase'.

headline.arc_game_adapters_in_scored_closure_note: VERIFIED independently, not taken from the docstring claim at scripts/arc_loop_solve.py:66-69. arc_game_adapters is absent from the 55-file E3 closure and present in the 129-file arc_loop_solve closure.

cross_game_priors_NOT_counted_as_leaks.rationale: These are distilled from the 25 public games but are NOT keyed on the current game id, and they SHIP inside the submission, so a hidden Kaggle game genuinely receives them too. Removing them would make the proxy PESSIMISTIC rather than faithful. Listed so the enumeration is not read as exhaustive of public-game influence.
items: models/arc_playbook_index/ (arc_playbook_retrieval.py:26) -- 25-game-distilled exploration patterns; the PATTERNS are game-agnostic, only the query TAGS are id-keyed (see B1)
ops/arc_router_ledger.json -- 12 public games, consumed as a trained model not a per-game row
registry general_gotchas (n=30) and derived cautions (n=8) -- MEASURED IDENTICAL for the public and hidden probe

disableability.single_highest_leverage_mitigation: Alias the game id at the POLICY boundary while keeping the true id at the ENV boundary. E3AgentPolicy performs no environment I/O with self.short, so passing a synthetic id disables A1-A7, B1, B2, B4(self-row) and C1-C6 in one change. This is not a hypothesis: constructing E3AgentPolicy('zz99hiddengame') already reproduces the hidden-game profile exactly (graph_explore, budget 80, confident_transfer False, no ranked recipes).
disableability.additional_required_switch: CARNOT_ARC_E3_DIR=<tmpdir>, exported BEFORE import, to stop B3 reading a stale results/arc_e3/<game>/world_model.py
disableability.residual_ceiling: C7 (environment_files/<game>) cannot be disabled because the offline twin is defined by it. Therefore an adapter-free offline run bounds a hidden game's performance from ABOVE, never measures it: the agent still gets a perfectly faithful, instantly-resettable, zero-latency simulator of a game whose source exists locally, which no hidden Kaggle game provides.

statistical_claims.min_reachable_p_note: NONE STATED AND NONE REACHABLE. This phase changed no behaviour and ran no comparative outcome measurement, so there is no test to pre-register. When the adapter-free measurement itself is run, the pre-registered bound must be computed at GAME clustering over the 25-game roster, and reported as min/q1/median/q3/max per game, never as a single headline.

limitations: Static closure analysis cannot see imports built by string construction or importlib at runtime; a lookup reached only that way would be missed. Two importlib sites were found and are accounted for (arc_executable_world_model.py:2365-2367, arc_competition_agent.py:623-626).

The delivery probe covers CONSTRUCTION only. Sites B1-B5 fire inside _induce_and_plan / _maybe_route_from_transitions and are reported as runtime-conditional, NOT as measured-delivered. They were not exercised because that requires a live generator and this run is CPU-only by design.
n=2 game ids in the delivery probe is a witness of differential behaviour, not a roster measurement.
D3 is in-closure with live invocation unestablished. It is reported as such rather than assumed either way.
verifier_is_oracle_note: No verifier claim is made. This artifact is an audit enumeration, not a solve or a moat claim.

corrections_2026_08_04.provenance: Adversarial review of exp6092, each correction re-verified independently before being applied. Prior values PRESERVED per the never-prune rule.

corrections.retracted: cross_game_priors_NOT_counted_as_leaks: 'registry general_gotchas (n=30) and derived cautions (n=8) -- MEASURED IDENTICAL for the public and hidden probe', and the same sentence in honest_verdict.
corrections.what_is_actually_true: Only the COUNT is identical. general_gotchas (n=30) IS byte-identical. cautions are n=8 in both cases but the CONTENT differs per game.
corrections.mechanism: arc_solve_learning.py:654-676 `_cautions_from` appends the top-3 RANKED games' dead_ends / dead_ends_recorded FIRST and reg['general_gotchas'] LAST, then caps at out[:8]. For a public game the ranked dead-ends fill the cap and the general gotchas are cut entirely. What a public game receives is per-game dead-end prose with literal solve coordinates -- sb26's first caution names a controlled marker at (15,36) and a target marker at (51,30).
corrections.the_ACTUAL_reason_cautions_are_not_count: They have NO consumer anywhere in either import closure. Produced at arc_solve_learning.py:766 (cold) and :849 (warm), referenced only inside the `guidance` prose string at :855/:859. approach_recommendation is read back by exactly one key -- ['strategy'] at arc_competition_agent.py:4631/:4642. So cautions are populated onto the policy and never read: an AVAILABILITY-IS-NOT-DELIVERY exclusion, not an identity exclusion. The report reached a defensible exclusion from a false measurement.
corrections.consequence_for_future_arms: Any future arm that keeps a real game id must record that cautions still carry ranked-game dead-end prose with literal solve coordinates, even though nothing currently consumes it. The identity claim must not be reused as justification for leaving them in.

corrections.read_at: scored-path construction: arc_competition_agent.py:4617 -> _load_submitted_frame_change_scorer (:1050) -> load_live_action_effect_scorer (arc_frame_change_predictor.py:484) -> load_cached_transition_effect_rows (:385, globs data/arc_transition_corpus/*.npz)
corrections.classification: NOT a leak -- a genuinely diluted cross-game prior. It globs all 25 games rather than keying on the target, aggregates to only 24 keys (8 action ids + 16 click buckets), and removing any single game shifts a ratio by at most 0.069 with no key lost. But the target game's OWN rows ARE folded in, because the scored call site passes no exclude_games (the parameter exists and defaults to ()), so the artifact's not-counted list was not exhaustive as written.
corrections.one_line_mitigation_not_previously_recor: exclude_games is an existing, unused parameter at the scored call site.
corrections.reviewer_figure_narrowed: The reviewer reported 176 rows with level_progress>0; measured here as 172.

corrections.retracted: method/headline: the arc_loop_solve closure recorded as 129 files.
corrections.note: 160, not 129 -- the 129 came from a narrower module-resolver scope that missed scripts/-rooted and repo-rooted modules. exp6093's own pre-registration already records 160. The LOAD-BEARING claim is unaffected and is independently confirmed here: the scored closure is 55 files and arc_game_adapters is ABSENT from it.

corrections.statement: Three independent sweeps of the 55-file scored closure (literal game-id regex over all 25 ids; lookup-shape regex; an ast sweep for game-id-shaped container literals and non-literal data paths) found no Tier-A-class site keyed on the target id beyond the seven enumerated -- which strengthens the enumeration. But all three are static analysis plus a construction-time probe. 'Enumerated' must not be read as 'closed': B1-B5 live inside _induce_and_plan / _maybe_route_from_transitions and remain UNMEASURED under a live generator; D3 (arc_solver_kit.py:4002) remains unestablished; and static closure analysis cannot see an import built by string construction (two importlib sites were found and accounted for, a third built some other way would have been missed).
